title: Fix plugin checks for wp.org
body:
We need to make sure the code base passed the plugin check ran by wp.org before we can submit the plugin for inclusion in the repository. 

It will be run as part of the review process or we can run it ourselves with the plugin [](https://wordpress.org/plugins/plugin-check/)

Basically it runs phpcs and reports any security problems. I find it easier just to run vendor/bin/phpcs as configured in the project to find security problems. I already fixed most of the escaping related ones but there are more to do.

Steps to complete this issue:
- [x] Run vendor/bin/phpcs 
- [x] Review WordPress.Security.EscapeOutput errors
- [x] Add esc_html, esc_attr, esc_url, or wp_kses if appropriate. Use `// phpcs:ignore WordPress.Security.EscapeOutput.OutputNotEscaped` if out really doesn't need escaped.
- [x] Review WordPress.Security.NonceVerification errors
- [x] Add [a nonce check if needed](https://developer.wordpress.org/news/2023/08/understand-and-use-wordpress-nonces-properly/). If the request makes any changes to the database or state then a check is needed, other was add `// phpcs:ignore WordPress.Security.NonceVerification`
- [x] Review WordPress.Security.ValidatedSanitizedInput errors
- [x] [Sanitize](https://developer.wordpress.org/apis/security/sanitizing/) All user inputs. Usually this looks like `sanitize_text_field(wp_unslash($_SERVER['HTTP_USER_AGENT'] ?? '')` but the sanitize function should match the type of input expected.

title: Add Domain > Primary Domains setting should have a warning of some kind
body: It's not entirely clear that the "Primary Domain" setting is a danger to users when adding new domains, as this sets the main domain for the entire WP Multisite WaaS. Suggest: 1. Renaming this to "Main WP Multisite WaaS Domain" 2. Changing the description to: "Set this as the main WaaS website domain" 3. Change the toggle button selected colour to Red. 4. Perhaps a warning pop-up: "Are you sure you want to change the main domain used for this WP Multisite WaaS website? There's further confusion when using Closte.com for hosting, and maybe others, where the term "Primary Domain" is used to choose between www. or non-www. So, too easy for users to mix these settings up with unintended consequences in changing and potential lock-out from their main website, with all the URLs changed, and no small task in restoring the correct main domain for the WaaS site. `/wp-admin/network/admin.php?page=wp-ultimo-domains` `//wp-admin/network/admin.php?page=wp-ultimo-edit-domain&id=13&model=domain`

title: Invoice Download with RTL languages
body: I wanted to use the plugin on an Arabic website -Arabic is an RTL language- and all worked well, but when I tried to download a customer invoice, I got this error "Your server's PHP and WordPress memory limits are too low to perform this check. You might need to contact your host provider and ask the PHP memory limit in particular to be raised." which did not make any sense because the memory limit was 512MB and when I switch the website back to english, the invoice is downloadable without any issues. After digging deeper, I found that the plugin misses a font TTF file in this path `wp-content/plugins/wp-multisite-waas/dependencies/mpdf/mpdf/ttfonts` The font is called XB_Riyaz.ttf. I used the Amiri font -as it should work with Arabic without any problem- and made some changes to this file "using AI" `class-invoice.php` in this path `wp-multisite-waas\inc\invoices`, and now I can download the invoice on an Arabic website, but the Arabic words have spaces between letters. The words should be like this فاتورة, but in the PDF it is ف ا ت و ر ة I will attach the PDF invoice and the new adjusted code. One last thing, I get this PHP warning related to the translation, it is something like the translation is loaded too early `[01-May-2025 07:41:20 UTC] PHP Notice: Function _load_textdomain_just_in_time was called incorrectly. Translation loading for the wp-ultimo domain was triggered too early. This is usually an indicator for some code in the plugin or theme running too early. Translations should be loaded at the init action or later. Please see Debugging in WordPress for more information. (This message was added in version 6.7.0.) in /var/www/html/wp-includes/functions.php on line 6121` [mpdf_23.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19997799/mpdf_23.pdf) [class-invoice-php.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19997804/class-invoice-php.txt)

title: PayPal checkout loops back to /register (sandbox). NVP capture fails with error 10002.
body:
Environment

WP Ultimo: [vX.Y.Z]

WordPress: [v6.8.x]

PHP: [7.4/8.x]

CDN/Proxy: Cloudflare (SSL/TLS Full (strict))

Multisite: Subdomain mode (WaaS)

**Gateway in use**

WP Ultimo – PayPal (Standard/Express – NVP) with Sandbox ON
(Settings show API Username / API Password / API Signature — not REST/PPCP.)

**Observed behavior**

Customer goes to /register, chooses a plan, clicks Finish Payment.

Redirects to sandbox.paypal.com, buyer approves.

After clicking “Pay now,” PayPal returns to:

https://example.com/register/?payment=[PAYMENT_CODE]&wu-confirm=paypal&token=EC-[...]&PayerID=[...]


The page loops/stays on /register; payment/subscription is not completed.

**Expected**

After the return, WP Ultimo should capture the payment and activate the subscription/site.

**What I already verified**

Return handler DOES run (mu-plugin log on init):

[UTC timestamp] WU PayPal RETURN: {"payment":"[PAYMENT_CODE]","wu-confirm":"paypal","token":"EC-[...]","PayerID":"[...]"}


IPN endpoint is reachable (for Standard/Express):

POST https://example.com/?wu-listener=paypal returns 200.

Log:

[UTC timestamp] WU PayPal LISTENER HIT (legacy IPN): {"wu-listener":"paypal"}


Server can reach PayPal NVP, but PayPal rejects the capture with 10002
(test call to https://api-3t.sandbox.paypal.com/nvp from the server):

ACK=Failure&L_ERRORCODE0=10002&L_SHORTMESSAGE0=Security error&L_LONGMESSAGE0=Security header is not valid


Log excerpt:

[UTC timestamp] WU NVP TEST CODE: 200
[UTC timestamp] WU NVP TEST BODY: ... ACK=Failure ... 10002 ... Security header is not valid


Cloudflare exclusions in place (so CF is not the cause):

Cache bypass + Rocket Loader/Minify OFF for: /register, /wp-json/*, /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php

WAF “Skip” for webhooks/listeners

Tested with Development Mode as well

Control tests on same server:

WooCommerce PayPal Payments (PPCP/REST) completes successfully (no loop).

Stripe in WP Ultimo completes successfully.

Interpretation

The loop occurs after the return, so the plugin’s capture step (NVP DoExpressCheckoutPayment) appears to fail.

PayPal’s 10002 means invalid NVP credentials or mode mismatch. I entered the sandbox seller account’s NVP Username/Password/Signature in WP Ultimo with Sandbox ON. If the gateway also requires a specific merchant email or PDT token, please confirm.

Questions

Please confirm this gateway is NVP/Express and list the exact required fields (NVP trio only? merchant email? PDT?).

Where can I enable verbose logging to capture the raw NVP response inside WP Ultimo instead of silently looping?

Are there known conditions that cause a redirect loop when NVP capture fails (e.g., missing admin-ajax call, nonce/session), or should the PayPal error be surfaced to the user/admin?

If the recommended path is PayPal Commerce (PPCP/REST), how do I enable that in WP Ultimo?

Hitting https://example.com/wp-json/wp-ultimo/v1/paypal/webhook currently returns 404, suggesting the PPCP route is not registered in my build.

Please provide the exact fields (Client ID/Secret, Webhook ID) and required webhook URL for PPCP in WP Ultimo.

Extras

Domain redacted: using https://example.com for all references.

Happy to provide a temporary admin login or full debug log if needed.

Thanks!

title: Email verification skipped on paid plans (accounts/site created before verification)
body:
Hi team,

I’m seeing inconsistent email-verification behavior with Multisite Ultimate and would appreciate guidance on whether this is expected, a bug, or a configuration gap.

Environment (placeholders):
Multisite: Enabled
Plugin: Multisite Ultimate
Payment/membership plugin: Stripe
Mailer: native

**Steps to reproduce:**

_Free plan registration_

User registers on {SIGNUP PAGE/flow}.

Verification email is sent.

Only after clicking the verification link, the site is created and user onboarding continues. ✅ (This is the behavior we want.)

_Paid plan registration (same flow, paid tier)_

User registers and proceeds to checkout.

No verification email is sent.

The system immediately creates the account, accepts payment, and creates the site.

If the email is mistyped, the user never receives anything but still has a paid account/site provisioned. ❌

**Expected behavior:**

Require email verification first, then proceed to payment and site creation (for all plans, free and paid).

At minimum, do not capture payment or create a site until the email address is confirmed.

**Actual behavior:**

Verification is enforced only for free plan registrations.

For paid plan registrations, verification is skipped and provisioning/payment occurs immediately.

**Impact:**

Risk of orphaned paid accounts/sites if the user mistypes their email.

Compliance/chargeback risk and poor UX (users don’t receive access emails).

**Questions / Requests:**

Is there a built-in setting to enforce email verification before checkout and site creation on paid plans?

If not, can you confirm this as a bug or provide the recommended hooks/filters to implement this officially? For example:

A hook to send/require verification in paid flows,

A gate to block payment processing until user_meta msu_verified === 1,

A gate to block site creation/provisioning until verification is complete.

If the intended design is “skip verification on paid plans,” could you share documentation or a roadmap item to support “verify-first” flows?

Thank you! I’m happy to test a patch or beta.

title: There is a login redirection issue affecting subsite users in a WordPress Multisite network using the plugin
body: When a user from a subsite tries to log in through the **main network login page** (for example, `https://hostingzella.com/login`), they are redirected to the **network dashboard** and see the following warning message: > You attempted to access the "Test Network" dashboard, but you do not currently have privileges on this site. If you believe you should be able to access the "Test Network" dashboard, please contact your network administrator. > > If you reached this screen by accident and meant to visit one of your own sites, here are some shortcuts to help you find your way. However, if the same user logs in **directly through their own subsite’s login page** (e.g., `https://hanoush583.hostingzella.com/wp-login.php`), the login works perfectly and they are redirected correctly to their subsite dashboard. This issue often occurs because users may reach the main network login page unintentionally — for example, when they use the “Forgot Password” or password reset flow, which automatically redirects them to the main site’s `/login` URL instead of their subsite’s login page. Expected behavior: * Subsite users who log in from the main domain should be redirected to their own subsite dashboard instead of the network dashboard, or at least shown a friendly redirect to their subsite instead of the privilege warning screen.

title: Offer Add-ons on Products no longer save in latest Ultimate Multisite
body:
Description:
I’m upgrading from WP Ultimo 2.3.3 where “Offer Add-ons” on Products (Plans) works correctly.

In 2.4.x (Ultimate Multisite), I can select a Service in the Offer Add-ons field on a Product and it shows as selected. After I click Save Product, the page reloads and the field is empty again.

Steps to reproduce:

Network install Ultimate Multisite 2.4.x on a fresh multisite.

Create a Service product.

Create a Plan product.

In the Plan, go to Up & Downgrades → Offer Add-ons and select the Service.

Click Save Product.

Reload the page.

Expected:
The selected Service remains saved in the Offer Add-ons field.

Actual:
The field is empty; no Offer Add-ons are saved.

Environment:

WP Ultimo / Ultimate Multisite: 2.4.x

WordPress:  6.8.3

PHP: 8.3.25

Tested on a clean network with only Ultimate Multisite active.

Same setup on WP Ultimo 2.3.3 works correctly (Offer Add-ons persist).

This appears to be a regression introduced after 2.3.3.

title: API : The `wu/v2` does not appear to support pagination or filtering via query parameters.
body:
The `wu/v2` API does not appear to support pagination or filtering via query parameters.

When using Bricks Builder (Query Loop type API) on the `/wu/v2/site` endpoint, standard parameters (`page`, `per_page`, `number`) are not taken into account — the response always returns all items regardless of pagination.

Additionally, the documentation lists endpoints in the plural form while the actual routes use the singular:
- Docs: `/wu/v2/sites`, `/wu/v2/customers`, `/wu/v2/memberships`…
- Actual: `/wu/v2/site`, `/wu/v2/customer`, `/wu/v2/membership`…

Ref: https://ultimatemultisite.com/docs/ro/developer/rest-api/overview/

**To Reproduce**

1. Call `GET /wp-json/wu/v2/site?page=1&per_page=5`
2. The response returns all sites with no limit applied
3. `X-WP-Total` and `X-WP-TotalPages` headers are missing or incorrect

**Expected behavior**

- Support for `page` and `per_page` (or `number`) parameters to paginate results
- `X-WP-Total` and `X-WP-TotalPages` headers present in the response
- Documentation updated to reflect singular route names

**Environment**

- Plugin: Ultimate Multisite
- API namespace: `wu/v2`
- Tested with: Bricks Builder Query Loop (API type)

`WordPress add_query_arg() encoding behavior parameter values`

💡 Result:

Short answer: add_query_arg() does not automatically encode parameter values — it expects values to be pre-encoded (urlencode() or rawurlencode()). If you pass unencoded values that contain & or =, they will be treated as additional query separators (possible parameter hijack). Use rawurlencode() (or array_map('rawurlencode', $args)) for values and late-escape the returned URL with esc_url(). [1][2]

Example:
- Wrong: add_query_arg( 'my_arg', 'a&b=1', $url ); // produces ...&my_arg=a&b=1 (broken)
- Right: add_query_arg( 'my_arg', rawurlencode('a&b=1'), $url ); // produces ...&my_arg=a%26b%3D1

🌐 Web query:

`WordPress add_query_arg() double encoding rawurlencode issue`

💡 Result:

Short answer: double-encoding happens when you feed add_query_arg() an already-encoded string (or an encoded URL) and then encode it again. Fixes: pass raw (unencoded) values to add_query_arg(), or if you have an encoded value decode it first and then encode exactly once. Sources and examples below.

Why it happens
- add_query_arg()/related functions expect query values to be URL-encoded in a single, consistent way; feeding already-encoded values (or an encoded URL) will produce %25 sequences (double-encoding) or incorrectly treat encoded ampersands as anchors. title: fix: SC2015 A&&B||C anti-pattern in bin/deploy.sh
body:
## Quality Debt: ShellCheck SC2015

**Source**: Daily quality sweep 2026-03-25
**File**: `bin/deploy.sh`
**Severity**: Error (SC2015)

### Finding

`Note that A && B || C is not if-then-else. C may run when A is true. [SC2015]`

The `A && B || C` pattern is not equivalent to `if A; then B; else C; fi`. If `B` exits non-zero, `C` will run unexpectedly. This can cause silent failures in deploy scripts.

### Fix

Replace `A && B || C` patterns with explicit `if/then/else` blocks:

```bash
# Before (buggy)
some_command && success_action || failure_action

# After (correct)
if some_command; then
  success_action
else
  failure_action
fi
```

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All SC2015 violations in `bin/deploy.sh` replaced with explicit if/then/else
- [ ] `shellcheck bin/deploy.sh` reports zero SC2015 violations
- [ ] Deploy script behaviour unchanged (test with dry-run if available)

title: REST API returns null for all meta-stored fields on Site and 6 other models
body:
## Bug Description

The REST API returns `null` for all meta-stored properties across 7 models. This makes the API unusable for retrieving critical data like `customer_id`, `membership_id`, `line_items`, etc.

## Root Cause

`Base_Model::to_array()` (line 840) uses `get_object_vars($this)` to serialize models. However, several models use **lazy-loaded properties** that are fetched from metadata tables only when their getter is called (e.g., `get_customer_id()` calls `$this->get_meta('wu_customer_id')`).

Since `to_array()` never calls these getters, the properties remain `null` in the serialized JSON response.

## Affected Models and Fields

| Model | Null Fields in API Response |
|-------|---------------------------|
| **Site** | `customer_id`, `membership_id`, `featured_image_id`, `categories` + `id` returns `0` instead of `blog_id` |
| **Product** | `featured_image_id`, `tax_category`, `contact_us_label`, `contact_us_link`, `feature_list`, `available_addons`, `legacy_options`, `pwyw_minimum_amount`, `pwyw_suggested_amount`, `pwyw_recurring_mode` |
| **Customer** | `has_trialed`, `extra_information` |
| **Payment** | `line_items`, `invoice_number` |
| **Checkout_Form** | `thank_you_page_id`, `conversion_snippets` |
| **Email** | `event`, `schedule` |
| **Broadcast** | `migrated_from_id`, `notice_type` |

**Note:** `Discount_Code` and `Event` already override `to_array()` and are not affected.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable the REST API in Ultimate Multisite settings
2. Call `GET /wp-json/wu/v2/site/{id}` with valid API credentials
3. Observe that `customer_id`, `membership_id`, `type`, `active`, etc. are all `null`
4. Same issue on `GET /wp-json/wu/v2/site?domain=example.com`

## Example API Response (Site)

```json
{
  "id": 0,
  "blog_id": "7",
  "domain": "www.example.com",
  "customer_id": null,
  "membership_id": null,
  "type": null,
  "active": null,
  "template_id": null,
  "featured_image_id": null,
  "categories": null
}
```

## Proposed Fix

Override `to_array()` in each affected model to call the lazy-loaded getters before calling `parent::to_array()`. This follows the existing pattern used by `Discount_Code` and `Event` models.

I'll submit a PR with the fix shortly.

title: REST API: meta-stored fields (type, customer_id) cannot be used as query filters on Site endpoint
body:
## Bug Description

The Site REST API endpoint (`GET /wu/v2/site`) does not support filtering by meta-stored fields like `type` and `customer_id`. For example, `?type=customer_owned` or `?customer_id=43` return **all** sites instead of filtered results.

## Root Cause

The Site model stores `type`, `customer_id`, `membership_id`, and other fields in `wp_blogmeta` (not as columns in `wp_blogs`). The underlying BerlinDB query engine can only filter by actual table columns. When these meta field names are passed as query parameters, BerlinDB silently ignores them.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable the REST API in Ultimate Multisite settings
2. Call `GET /wp-json/wu/v2/site?type=customer_owned`
3. Observe that **all** sites are returned, not just `customer_owned` sites
4. Same issue with `?customer_id=43`

## Expected Behavior

- `?type=customer_owned` should return only sites with `type = customer_owned`
- `?customer_id=43` should return only sites owned by customer 43
- `?membership_id=94` should return only sites linked to membership 94

## Possible Solutions

1. Override `Site_Query::query()` to convert `type`, `customer_id`, `membership_id` params into `meta_query` clauses
2. Add post-query filtering in `get_items_rest()` for meta-stored fields (less efficient but simpler)
3. Add these as proper columns to a custom sites table (breaking change)

## Affected Fields

| Field | Storage | Filterable? |
|-------|---------|------------|
| `domain` | `wp_blogs` column | ✅ Yes |
| `path` | `wp_blogs` column | ✅ Yes |
| `blog_id` | `wp_blogs` column | ✅ Yes |
| `type` | `wp_blogmeta` | ❌ No |
| `customer_id` | `wp_blogmeta` | ❌ No |
| `membership_id` | `wp_blogmeta` | ❌ No |
| `template_id` | `wp_blogmeta` | ❌ No |

## Related

- #469 — REST API returns null for meta-stored fields (fix merged)
- Pagination fix in progress (separate PR)

title: REST API: per_page and page parameters are ignored, no X-WP-Total headers
body:
## Bug Description

The REST API does not support standard WP REST pagination parameters (`per_page`, `page`). These parameters are passed directly to BerlinDB which expects `number` and `offset` instead. Additionally, no `X-WP-Total` or `X-WP-TotalPages` response headers are sent.

## Root Cause

In `inc/apis/trait-rest-api.php`, `get_items_rest()` passes all request parameters directly to `::query()` without converting WP REST conventions to BerlinDB conventions:

- `per_page` → should map to `number`
- `page` → should be converted to `offset` = (page - 1) * number
- `X-WP-Total` / `X-WP-TotalPages` headers are never set

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Call \`GET /wp-json/wu/v2/site?per_page=1&page=1\`
2. Observe that **all** sites are returned (per_page is ignored)
3. Check response headers — no X-WP-Total or X-WP-TotalPages

## Expected Behavior

- \`?per_page=2&page=1\` returns 2 items
- \`?per_page=2&page=2\` returns the next 2 items
- Response headers include \`X-WP-Total: 7\` and \`X-WP-TotalPages: 4\`

## Impact

This breaks pagination in clients that follow the WP REST API standard, including:
- **Bricks Builder** API Loop (expects `per_page`, `page`, and `header.x-wp-totalpages`)
- Any standard WP REST client

## Workaround

Using BerlinDB native parameters works: `?number=2&offset=0`

## Proposed Fix

Convert WP REST params to BerlinDB format in `get_items_rest()` and add pagination headers via a count query. PR incoming.

## Related

- #469 — REST API returns null for meta-stored fields
- #479 — Meta fields cannot be used as query filters

title: REST API: description returns null, notes and limitations not JSON-serializable
body:
## Bug Description

PR #470 fixed most meta-stored fields returning `null` in REST API responses, but 3 fields are still broken:

### 1. `description` returns `null`

`Site::to_array()` does not call `get_description()`, which lazy-loads from `get_blog_option($id, 'blogdescription')`. The raw `$description` property stays `null`.

**Expected:** `"My site description"`
**Actual:** `null`

### 2. `notes` returns `[[], []]` instead of note content

`get_notes()` returns an array of `WP_Ultimo\Objects\Note` objects. The `Note` class has a `to_array()` method but does **not** implement `JsonSerializable`. When `json_encode()` serializes a `Note` object, it only sees public properties — but `$attributes` is `protected`, so the result is `{}` / `[]`.

**Expected:** `[{"text": "My note", "author_id": 1, "note_id": "abc123"}]`
**Actual:** `[[], []]`

### 3. `limitations` returns `[]` instead of limitations data

`get_limitations()` returns a `WP_Ultimo\Objects\Limitations` object. The class has `__serialize()` (for PHP's `serialize()`) but does **not** implement `JsonSerializable`. So `json_encode()` sees no public properties and returns `[]`.

**Expected:** `{"post_types": {"enabled": true, ...}, "plugins": {...}, ...}`
**Actual:** `[]`

## Proposed Fix

1. **Site `to_array()`**: Add `$array['description'] = $this->get_description();`
2. **Note class**: Implement `JsonSerializable` with `jsonSerialize()` calling `$this->to_array()`
3. **Limitations class**: Implement `JsonSerializable` with `jsonSerialize()` calling `$this->to_array()`

This follows the same pattern as the existing `__serialize()` method in Limitations.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a site with a description, notes, and limitations configured
2. Call `GET /wp-json/wu/v2/site/{id}`
3. Observe `description: null`, `notes: [[], []]`, `limitations: []`

title: bug(setup): Default Content wizard fails — Currency required, Unknown format specifier, causing NaN prices
body:
## Bug Description

The setup wizard's "Default Content" step fails on two items, causing cascading issues throughout the admin:

1. **Create Example Products** → `The Currency field is required`
2. **Create a Checkout Form** → `Unknown format specifier """`

### Root Cause

The wizard creates products/checkout forms before the currency setting is fully initialized. The `precision` setting is stored as an empty string `""` instead of the default `2`, and the currency validation fails during product creation.

### Cascading Effects

Because the wizard partially fails:

- **NaN€ prices everywhere in admin** — `precision: ""` → `parseFloat("")` → `NaN` in `wu_format_money()` JS function (`assets/js/functions.js:467`)
- **Products created with incorrect defaults** — `pricing_type: "free"`, `amount: 0` even for paid plans
- **Memberships created manually afterwards** have `user_id: 0` (possibly due to incomplete setup context)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Fresh WordPress multisite install
2. Install Ultimate Multisite from `main` branch
3. Network activate the plugin
4. Follow the setup wizard through to "Default Content" step
5. Observe: "Create Example Products" shows `The Currency field is required`
6. Observe: "Create a Checkout Form" shows `Unknown format specifier """`
7. Complete the wizard
8. Go to any membership/product edit page → prices show as `NaN€`

### Workaround

After completing the wizard, go to **Settings → General → Currency Options** and manually set:
- Currency: EUR (or desired currency)
- Precision: `2`
- Save

This fixes the NaN display, but the example products remain misconfigured.

### Environment

- WordPress 6.x multisite
- Ultimate Multisite `main` branch (post v2.4.12)
- PHP 8.2+

### Suggested Fix

The wizard should ensure currency settings (especially `precision`) are saved with proper defaults before creating products and checkout forms. The `precision` field should default to `2` (integer) instead of `""` (empty string) when not explicitly set.

title: feat(tax): universal tax fallback — implement as 'Apply to all countries' country dropdown option
body:
## Background

PR #277 (feat(tax): add universal tax fallback feature) was closed without merge. The maintainer (@superdav42) requested a different implementation approach.

## Requested Implementation

Instead of a separate settings toggle + rate field, implement universal/fallback tax as an **'Apply to all countries'** option in the existing country dropdown on the Tax Rates configuration page.

When a user selects 'Apply to all countries', the rate applies as a fallback when no country-specific rate matches.

## Original PR scope (for reference)
- PR #277 added `enable_universal_tax` toggle + `universal_tax_rate` field (0-100%)
- Maintainer feedback: use the existing country dropdown UX instead
- Branch was deleted; code needs to be reimplemented per the new approach

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] 'Apply to all countries' option added to country dropdown on Tax Rates page
- [ ] Rate configured via this option applies as fallback when no country-specific rate matches
- [ ] Translations updated for new strings
- [ ] Existing country-specific rates take precedence over the universal fallback

title: fix(security): replace wp_redirect with wp_safe_redirect in class-primary-domain.php
body:
## Problem

`inc/domain-mapping/class-primary-domain.php:109` uses `wp_redirect()` with a `// phpcs:ignore` suppression instead of `wp_safe_redirect()`.

```php
// TODO: Use wp_safe_redirect
wp_redirect(set_url_scheme($new_url)); // phpcs:ignore WordPress.Security.SafeRedirect.wp_redirect_wp_redirect
```

`wp_redirect()` does not validate that the redirect target is a safe URL, which can allow open redirect vulnerabilities if `$new_url` is ever influenced by untrusted input. `wp_safe_redirect()` validates the host against the allowed list.

## Solution

Replace `wp_redirect()` with `wp_safe_redirect()` and remove the phpcs:ignore suppression. Since this is a domain mapping redirect (replacing the current URL's host with a mapped domain), the target URL is derived from the site's own domain configuration — but using the safe variant is still the correct practice and removes the lint suppression.

If `wp_safe_redirect()` rejects the mapped domain (e.g., because it's not in the allowed hosts list), add the mapped domain to the allowed hosts via the `allowed_redirect_hosts` filter.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wp_redirect` replaced with `wp_safe_redirect` in `class-primary-domain.php:109`
- [ ] phpcs:ignore comment removed
- [ ] Redirect still works for mapped domains (add `allowed_redirect_hosts` filter if needed)
- [ ] Unit test added or updated to cover the redirect path

title: feat(addon): create multisite-ultimate-fluentaffiliate addon for recurring commission tracking
body:
## Background

Issue #185 (FluentAffiliate integration request) was reviewed and approved with conditions. This task implements the approved solution.

## What

Create a new addon `multisite-ultimate-fluentaffiliate` (or `ultimate-multisite-fluentaffiliate`) that:

1. **Recurring commission tracking**: Stores affiliate ID on membership at signup (from FluentAffiliate cookie/session), then fires a commission on each renewal payment via the `wu_create_payment` hook or payment model post-save.
2. **Manual affiliate assignment**: Adds a meta field to the membership edit admin page (`class-membership-edit-admin-page.php`) for manual affiliate assignment.

## Pre-implementation requirement

**Verify FluentAffiliate has a public PHP API for programmatic commission creation** (e.g., `fluentaffiliate_add_commission()` or similar). If no such API exists, this task is blocked upstream — open a feature request with WPManageNinja first and close this issue as blocked.

## Architecture

- Mirror the existing AffiliateWP addon (`multisite-ultimate-affiliatewp`) pattern
- Store affiliate ID as membership meta at signup
- Hook at the payment model layer (after `wu_create_payment`), not at the Stripe gateway layer — so it works with PayPal and other gateways
- Renewal payment hook point: `inc/gateways/class-base-stripe-gateway.php:3010` (transaction_type = 'renewal')

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] FluentAffiliate PHP API verified (document the API function used)
- [ ] Addon created following `ultimate-multisite-addon-template` pattern
- [ ] Affiliate ID stored on membership at signup from FluentAffiliate cookie/session
- [ ] Commission fired on renewal payments (gateway-agnostic)
- [ ] Manual affiliate assignment field on membership edit admin page
- [ ] Works with both Stripe and PayPal gateways
- [ ] Unit tests for commission tracking logic

## References

- Issue #185 (approved with conditions)
- Existing AffiliateWP addon: `multisite-ultimate-affiliatewp`

title: fix(tours): wu_tours is not defined on network dashboard
body:
## Bug

```
Uncaught ReferenceError: wu_tours is not defined
    at HTMLDocument.<anonymous> (tours.js:7:10)
```

The guided tour on the network admin dashboard (`/wp-admin/network/`) throws a `ReferenceError` because `wu_tours` is never defined.

## Root Cause

`tours.js` line 7 calls `_.each(wu_tours, ...)` unconditionally. The `wu_tours` variable is localized onto the `wu-admin` script handle (`wp_localize_script('wu-admin', 'wu_tours', ...)` in `Tours::enqueue_scripts()` line 95).

Since PR #433 (`cb5a40fd` — "Scope admin asset enqueues to WP Ultimo pages only"), `wu-admin` is only enqueued on pages where `wu_is_wu_page()` returns true. The network dashboard (`index.php`, hook suffix `dashboard-network`) is **not** a WU page, so `wu-admin` is never enqueued there and `wu_tours` is never defined.

The code comment on line 94 says _"wu-admin which will always be there"_ — this assumption was broken by the performance scoping change.

## Affected Pages

- Network admin dashboard (`/wp-admin/network/`) — `Dashboard_Widgets::register_network_widgets()` creates a "dashboard" tour at line 104

Other pages that create tours (`class-dashboard-admin-page.php`, `class-product-edit-admin-page.php`, etc.) are WU pages where `wu-admin` IS enqueued, so they're unaffected.

## Fix Options

1. **In `Tours::enqueue_scripts()`**: Instead of localizing onto `wu-admin`, enqueue a lightweight carrier script (or use `wp_add_inline_script` on `underscore`) to define `wu_tours` and `wu_tours_vars` as globals. This decouples tours from `wu-admin`.

2. **In `tours.js`**: Add a guard `if (typeof wu_tours === 'undefined') return;` before the `_.each` call. This prevents the error but means tours silently won't work if the localization is missing — the underlying localization issue still needs fixing.

3. **In `Dashboard_Widgets::enqueue_scripts()`**: Explicitly enqueue `wu-admin` on the dashboard (like was done for `wu-functions`). This is the simplest fix but re-loads `wu-admin` on a non-WU page, partially undoing the performance optimization.

Option 1 is the cleanest — it fixes the architectural issue (tours shouldn't depend on `wu-admin` being present).

## Related

- PR #705 fixed the same class of bug for `wu_moment` / `activity-stream.js`
- Both regressions were introduced by #433 (`cb5a40fd`)

title: feat: Add Transactional_Email_Capability interface and Amazon SES core integration
body:
## Summary

Add a new capability interface for **transactional email delivery** (distinct from the existing `Email_Selling_Capability` which provisions mailboxes). This enables the core plugin to manage how WordPress sends outbound email (password resets, WooCommerce notifications, admin alerts) on a per-site basis, with automatic domain verification.

## Problem

Currently, transactional email delivery is configured at the server level (ssmtp/Postfix) and is invisible to the multisite platform. This creates several problems:

1. **From-address mismatch**: All sites send from the server's configured address, not their own domain -- hurting deliverability and brand trust
2. **No domain verification automation**: Adding a new site requires manual DNS record setup for SPF/DKIM
3. **No per-site sending control**: Can't throttle, monitor, or disable sending per site
4. **Provider lock-in**: Changing email providers requires server-level reconfiguration

## Proposed Solution

### 1. New `Transactional_Email_Capability` interface

Location: `inc/integrations/capabilities/interface-transactional-email-capability.php`

This is a **separate concern** from `Email_Selling_Capability` (which provisions mailboxes). Transactional email is about *delivery routing*, not mailbox management.

```php
interface Transactional_Email_Capability {
    public function verify_domain(string $domain): array;
    public function get_domain_verification_status(string $domain): array;
    public function get_domain_dns_records(string $domain): array;
    public function send_email(string $from, string $to, string $subject, string $body, array $headers = []): array;
    public function get_sending_statistics(string $domain, string $period = '24h'): array;
    public function set_sending_quota(string $domain, int $max_per_day): array;
    public function test_connection();
}
```

### 2. Hook into `wp_mail` per site

The core should provide a filter/action system that allows the active transactional email provider to intercept `wp_mail()` calls and route them through the configured provider, using the correct from-address for the current site's domain.

### 3. Domain lifecycle hooks

Fire events when domains are added/removed from the multisite so addons (email, domain seller) can react:

- `wu_domain_added` -- trigger domain verification in SES
- `wu_domain_removed` -- optionally clean up verified identity
- `wu_domain_verified` -- domain DNS records confirmed

### 4. Settings UI

Admin settings page section for selecting and configuring the transactional email provider, similar to how host provider integrations work today.

## Architecture Notes

- The existing `Integration` base class and `Integration_Registry` should be reused
- AWS SigV4 signing already exists in the WorkMail integration (`Amazon_WorkMail_Integration::sign_request()`) -- extract to a shared `AWS_Signer` trait or utility class for reuse by SES
- The `DNS_Provider_Interface` in `inc/integrations/host-providers/` can be leveraged to auto-create verification DNS records when the domain's DNS is managed by a supported provider (e.g., Cloudflare)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `Transactional_Email_Capability` interface defined with methods above
- [ ] Domain lifecycle hooks (`wu_domain_added`, `wu_domain_removed`, `wu_domain_verified`) firing at appropriate points
- [ ] `wp_mail` interception mechanism that routes through the active provider with correct from-address
- [ ] Settings UI for provider selection and configuration
- [ ] AWS SigV4 signing extracted to reusable utility (shared with WorkMail)
- [ ] Documentation for addon developers to implement the interface

## Related

- Email addon: will implement `Amazon_SES_Email_Selling` (separate issue)
- Domain seller addon: will hook `wu_domain_added` to auto-verify (separate issue)
- Existing: `Email_Selling_Capability` (mailbox provisioning -- different concern)
- Existing: `DNS_Provider_Interface` (can auto-create DNS records)

title: fix(dashboard): enqueue wu-styling on network admin dashboard for activity-stream widget
body:
## Problem

The activity-stream dashboard widget wraps its output in `<div class="wu-styling">`, which requires `framework.css` (registered as the `wu-styling` stylesheet handle). The network admin dashboard (`index.php`) is not a wp-ultimo admin page, so `enqueue_default_admin_styles()` skips it — the stylesheet is never enqueued, causing the widget to render unstyled.

## Fix

Add `wp_enqueue_style('wu-styling')` in `Dashboard_Widgets::enqueue_scripts()` before the existing script enqueues. This method already guards on `$pagenow === 'index.php'`, so the enqueue only fires on the dashboard.

## Files Changed

- EDIT: `inc/class-dashboard-widgets.php` — add `wp_enqueue_style('wu-styling')` in `enqueue_scripts()`

## Verification

Activate the plugin on a WordPress Multisite install, visit the network admin dashboard, and confirm the activity-stream widget renders with correct styling (borders, typography, colours from the wu-styling framework).

title: Domain mapping: missing option_home filter + no rewrite flush after site duplication
body:
## Summary

Three related bugs in domain mapping that cause **404 errors on custom post types**, **broken Elementor preview**, and **mixed content issues** on subsites with mapped domains.

Discovered on a production multisite with 200+ subsites, affecting 8 sites simultaneously.

## Bug 1: Missing `option_home` filter in Domain_Mapping (CRITICAL)

**File:** `inc/class-domain-mapping.php` ~line 493

The `register_filters()` method adds `option_siteurl` but **not** `option_home`:

```php
add_filter('site_url', [$this, 'mangle_url'], -10, 4);
add_filter('home_url', [$this, 'mangle_url'], -10, 4);
add_filter('option_siteurl', [$this, 'mangle_url'], 20);
// ❌ MISSING: add_filter('option_home', [$this, 'mangle_url'], 20);
```

**Impact:** `get_option('home')` returns the raw subdomain URL instead of the mapped domain. Since `get_permalink()` uses `home_url()` which falls back to `get_option('home')`, all internal links point to the wrong domain. This breaks:
- Course/CPT permalink resolution → 404
- Elementor iframe preview → cross-origin block
- Admin AJAX → mixed content (http vs https)
- Media library "Load More" button → AJAX fails

**Fix:** Add `add_filter('option_home', [$this, 'mangle_url'], 20);` after line 493.

## Bug 2: No `flush_rewrite_rules()` after `wu_duplicate_site`

When UM duplicates a template site, the `rewrite_rules` option is copied verbatim from the template. If the template's rewrite rules were generated with a different CPT slug (e.g., `cursos/` plural) and later changed to `curso/` (singular), all cloned subsites keep the stale rules.

**Impact:** Custom post type URLs return 404 because the rewrite rules don't match the registered CPT slugs.

**Fix:** Add a hook on `wu_duplicate_site` (or in `class-elementor-compat.php` where `regenerate_css` already hooks):

```php
add_action('wu_duplicate_site', function($new_site_id) {
    switch_to_blog((int) $new_site_id);
    flush_rewrite_rules(true);
    restore_current_blog();
}, 20);
```

## Bug 3: `fix_new_site_url_scheme()` not reliable

**File:** `inc/compat/class-general-compat.php` line 489

The function correctly checks the main site scheme and sets `https://` on new sites. However, on our production install, **8 subsites** were created with `http://` in both `home` and `siteurl`. 

This may be a race condition where the main site's `home_url()` returns `http://` during the site creation process (before SSL redirect kicks in), or the filter runs before the main site's options are fully loaded.

**Suggestion:** Consider hardcoding HTTPS if `is_ssl()` returns true at the network level, or checking `FORCE_SSL_ADMIN` / the actual request scheme as a fallback.

## Environment

- WordPress 6.9 Multisite (subdomain mode)
- Ultimate Multisite beta.20 (production)
- LiteSpeed + Cloudflare
- PHP 8.3

## Workaround

We deployed two mu-plugins as temporary fixes:
1. `kp-fix-um-domain-mapping.php` — adds the missing `option_home` filter, flushes rewrite rules on `wu_duplicate_site`, and enforces HTTPS on `wp_initialize_site`
2. `kp-fix-subsite-rewrite.php` — intercepts WordPress's generic catch-all rewrite rules that match before CPT-specific rules (a WP core issue with `use_verbose_page_rules` in subdomain multisite)

Happy to submit a PR with the fixes if that helps.

title: chore: upgrade GitHub Actions from Node.js 20 to Node.js 24
body:
## Problem

GitHub Actions is deprecating Node.js 20. Actions running on Node.js 20 will be forced to Node.js 24 starting **June 2, 2026**, and Node.js 20 will be removed from runners on **September 16, 2026**.

This repo's workflows use actions that still run on Node.js 20, producing deprecation warnings on every run.

## Required upgrades

| Current | Upgrade to |
|---------|------------|
| `actions/download-artifact@v4` | `actions/download-artifact@v8` |
| `actions/upload-artifact@v4` | `actions/upload-artifact@v7` |

`shivammathur/setup-php@v2` is already on Node 24 (v2.37.0) -- no change needed.

## How

EDIT: `.github/workflows/*.yml` -- find-and-replace the action version tags per the table above.

For `softprops/action-gh-release`, add this env var to the workflow or job level until upstream releases a Node 24 version:

```yaml
env:
  FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24: true
```

## Verification

After merging, trigger a workflow run and confirm no Node.js 20 deprecation warnings appear in the annotations.

## References

- [GitHub blog: Deprecation of Node 20 on GitHub Actions runners](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-09-19-deprecation-of-node-20-on-github-actions-runners/)

title: t205: Setup AppArmor profile for FrankenPHP WordPress multisite
body:
## What

Create and deploy an AppArmor profile for the FrankenPHP WordPress multisite process.

**Scope:**
1. AppArmor profile for FrankenPHP worker process:
   - Read-only: plugin/theme/core dirs
   - Write-only: uploads/cache/tmp/sessions
   - Deny: exec/process spawning, access outside site root, sensitive paths (`/etc/shadow`, `/root`, `/home`, SSH keys, other vhosts)
   - Network: restrict to TCP 443+3306 only
2. Trellis Ansible role to deploy profile to `/etc/apparmor.d/` on production
3. Deploy in complain mode first, run `aa-logprof` after 1 week to refine, then switch to enforce
4. Document FrankenPHP-specific considerations (FrankenPHP embeds PHP in Caddy — single Go binary, profile targets `caddy`/`frankenphp` binary not `php-fpm`)
5. Assess per-site PHP-FPM pool isolation feasibility for multisite (likely not viable — document why)

## Why

AppArmor mandatory access control limits blast radius if a plugin or theme is compromised. FrankenPHP's embedded architecture requires a custom profile (not a standard php-fpm profile).

## How

**Files to create:**
- NEW: `trellis/roles/apparmor-frankenphp/tasks/main.yml` — Ansible role
- NEW: `trellis/roles/apparmor-frankenphp/templates/frankenphp.j2` — AppArmor profile template
- NEW: `docs/security/apparmor-frankenphp.md` — FrankenPHP-specific documentation

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Site serves all domains with zero denials for legitimate operations
- [ ] Enforce mode blocks `exec()` and write-to-plugin-dirs
- [ ] Trellis role deploys profile idempotently

title: t509: fix: template_selection validation never fires — field ID maps to wrong rule key
body:
## What

The `template_selection` checkout field submits its value as `template_id` in POST data, but the validation rule lookup used `field['id']` (i.e. `template_selection`) directly. Since no validation rule exists under the key `template_selection`, the `required` check never fires — allowing checkout to proceed with no template selected.

Additionally, Rakit's `required` rule treats integer `0` as "present", so even a correctly-keyed rule would accept `template_id=0`. The fix adds `min:1` for `template_id` specifically.

Also fixes the validation error label from "Template ID" → "Template Selection" for better UX.

## Changes (uncommitted in worktree bugfix/template-validation)

- EDIT: `inc/checkout/class-checkout.php` — add `$field_to_rule_key` map, use mapped key for rule lookup, add `min:1` for `template_id`, fix label string

## Acceptance Criteria

- Checkout with a required template selection field and no template chosen shows a validation error
- `template_id=0` is rejected when `template_selection` field has `required` attribute
- Validation error reads "Template Selection" not "Template ID"

## Verification

```bash
# Manual: set a checkout form with required template_selection, submit without selecting
# Expected: validation error shown reading "Template Selection"
```

title: bug: addon-integration-test.yml workflow fails on every push (workflow file issue)
body:
## Problem

The reusable workflow `.github/workflows/addon-integration-test.yml` is failing on **every push** to `main` and other branches with GitHub's message: *"This run likely failed because of a workflow file issue."*

Confirmed failing runs (event: `push`):
- Run #24313710389 — branch: `main`
- Run #24313684212 — branch: `bugfix/elementor-kit-duplication`
- Run #24313624887 — branch: `bugfix/elementor-kit-duplication`
- Run #24298415003 — branch: `main`

The workflow is defined as `on: workflow_call` only (reusable, called by addon repos), but it is being triggered via `push` events on the core repo. GitHub is unable to evaluate the workflow file in this context — likely because the required input `addon-slug` has no value when invoked via push.

## Root Cause Hypothesis

The workflow file is being triggered by push events to the core repo, but since it's `workflow_call`-only with a required `addon-slug` input, GitHub fails to parse/evaluate it. This could be caused by:

1. A GitHub Actions bug where `workflow_call` reusable workflows appear in check suites for push events on the referenced repo when called by an addon
2. A misconfiguration in an addon repo calling this workflow without the required input
3. The workflow file was recently changed and now has a YAML syntax/schema issue

## Impact

- Persistent red check on every push to main and any branch
- Noise in CI — developers see failing checks that aren't actionable
- Risk of masking real failures

## Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.github/workflows/addon-integration-test.yml` — investigate trigger config, add `workflow_dispatch` with defaults for manual testing, or add guard step that skips when `addon-slug` is empty

## Verification

After fix: `gh run list --repo Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite --limit 10 --json conclusion,workflowName` — no `failure` for `addon-integration-test.yml`

title: [BUG] Site duplication still loses postmeta for nav_menu_item, attachment, elementor_library, and Kit (post-PR #803) — production patch ready to integrate
body:
## TL;DR

PR #803 (merged) fixes Kit URL replacement, but customer purchases at https://kursopro.com (production WP Ultimo multisite, ~250+ subsites) **still produce broken clones daily**. Customers see wrong colors, missing logos, broken menus, "TU LOGO AQUÍ" placeholders.

I built a 774-line mu-plugin (`kp-elementor-css-on-clone.php` v2.9) that patches everything on our end. **It's been running in production since 2026-04-13 with zero failures.** I'd love for this logic to live inside Multisite Ultimate natively so I can retire the patch.

**Full code (production-tested):** https://gist.github.com/kenedytorcatt/7a0341f56a092466a3a039463a2518c7

---

## The 4 bugs that survive PR #803

After `MUCD_Data::copy_data()` finishes (regardless of whether it's called via `MUCD_Duplicate::duplicate_blog()` or via WP Ultimo's `class-site-duplicator.php`), these postmeta rows are missing in the cloned site:

### Bug 1 — Kit `_elementor_page_settings` not fully copied
- **Symptom:** clone uses default Elementor blue (#6EC1E4) instead of template colors
- **Real case:** customer "bellaklin" (blog 296) cloned from template 97 → got default blue instead of pink (#EAC7C7, #ED6363)
- **Diagnosis:** template kit post 3 has 6387 bytes, clone had 5639 bytes (missing `system_colors` + `custom_colors` arrays)
- **Why PR #803 doesn't fix it:** PR #803 fixes URL replacement passes, but doesn't address the case where the postmeta row gets created with default Elementor stub data BEFORE copy_data runs, then copy_data uses `INSERT NOT EXISTS` and silently skips overwriting

### Bug 2 — `nav_menu_item` postmeta not copied
- **Symptom:** menus render as empty `<li>` tags with no titles, no URLs
- **Diagnosis:** nav_menu_item POSTS are copied (same IDs preserved) but their postmeta rows are NOT
- **Missing keys:** `_menu_item_type`, `_menu_item_object_id`, `_menu_item_object`, `_menu_item_url`, `_menu_item_menu_item_parent`, `_menu_item_target`, `_menu_item_classes`, `_menu_item_xfn`

### Bug 3 — `attachment` postmeta not copied
- **Symptom:** logos, default icons, Kit images render as broken/missing
- **Missing keys:** `_wp_attached_file`, `_wp_attachment_metadata`, `_wp_attachment_image_alt`

### Bug 4 — `elementor_library` CPT postmeta not copied
- **Symptom:** custom headers, footers, popups render as skeletons or default placeholder text
- **Real case:** clone of "plantilla4" → shopmariana.kursopro.com showed "TU LOGO AQUI" text instead of header logo
- **Diagnosis:** plantilla4 has 43 posts with `_elementor_data`, clone had only 10 (13 elementor_library templates were missing all postmeta)

---

## Critical insight (took me a week to figure out)

WP Ultimo customer purchases do **NOT** fire `mucd_after_copy_data` because `class-site-duplicator.php` calls `MUCD_Data::copy_data()` directly (not `MUCD_Duplicate::duplicate_blog()`). Instead, WP Ultimo fires its own `wu_duplicate_site` hook AFTER duplication.

This means:
- The correct hook for WP Ultimo flows is `wu_duplicate_site` (priority must be **before** your `Elementor_Compat::regenerate_css` which runs at default 10)
- `mucd_after_copy_data` only fires for manual admin duplications
- Both paths need coverage

Also: **the source template ID passed to MUCD's hooks is hardcoded by the duplication call**, but the customer's REAL template choice is in `get_site_meta($to, 'wu_template_id')`. Always prefer the meta over hook params.

---

## How to integrate this into Multisite Ultimate natively

I'm not asking you to copy my mu-plugin verbatim. Here's the minimum integration that would let me retire it:

### Step 1 — In `class-site-duplicator.php`, after `MUCD_Data::copy_data()` returns, run a postmeta backfill pass:

```php
// Pseudo-code — adapt to your codebase style
$this->backfill_missing_postmeta($from_site_id, $to_site_id, [
    'nav_menu_item' => [
        '_menu_item_type', '_menu_item_object_id', '_menu_item_object',
        '_menu_item_url', '_menu_item_menu_item_parent', '_menu_item_target',
        '_menu_item_classes', '_menu_item_xfn',
    ],
    'attachment' => [
        '_wp_attached_file', '_wp_attachment_metadata', '_wp_attachment_image_alt',
    ],
    'elementor_library' => '_elementor_*', // wildcard match
    'page' => '_elementor_*',
    'post' => '_elementor_*',
]);

$this->backfill_active_kit_settings($from_site_id, $to_site_id);
```

### Step 2 — `backfill_active_kit_settings()` implementation:

```php
private function backfill_active_kit_settings($from_site_id, $to_site_id) {
    switch_to_blog($from_site_id);
    $kit_id_from = (int) get_option('elementor_active_kit', 3);
    $kit_settings = get_post_meta($kit_id_from, '_elementor_page_settings', true);
    restore_current_blog();

    if (empty($kit_settings)) return;

    switch_to_blog($to_site_id);
    $kit_id_to = (int) get_option('elementor_active_kit', 3);
    // CRITICAL: must be update_post_meta (overwrite) — not INSERT NOT EXISTS
    update_post_meta($kit_id_to, '_elementor_page_settings', $kit_settings);
    delete_post_meta($kit_id_to, '_elementor_css'); // force regen
    if (class_exists('\Elementor\Core\Files\CSS\Post')) {
        (new \Elementor\Core\Files\CSS\Post($kit_id_to))->update();
    }
    restore_current_blog();
}
```

### Step 3 — Add post-clone verification (catches edge cases):

```php
// After backfill, verify the kit settings actually got copied
private function verify_kit_integrity($from_site_id, $to_site_id) {
    // compare bytes of _elementor_page_settings between source and clone
    // if clone < 80% of source bytes -> re-run backfill + schedule retry
}
```

### Step 4 — In `class-site-duplicator.php`, when resolving the source for cloning:

```php
// Always prefer wu_template_id meta over the explicit param
$meta_template = (int) get_site_meta($to_site_id, 'wu_template_id', true);
if ($meta_template > 0) {
    $from_site_id = $meta_template;
}
```

This eliminates the hardcoded source bug where MUCD passes a different blog ID than the customer actually selected.

---

## Reference implementation

Full production code in this Gist (774 lines, copy whatever you need):
https://gist.github.com/kenedytorcatt/7a0341f56a092466a3a039463a2518c7

Key functions to look at:
- `kp_run_complete_clone_fix()` — universal entry point with double-execution guard
- `kp_fix_kit_postmeta_on_clone()` — Bug 1 fix (uses `update_post_meta` not INSERT)
- `kp_fix_nav_menu_postmeta_on_clone()` — Bug 2 fix
- `kp_fix_attachment_postmeta_on_clone()` — Bug 3 fix
- `kp_fix_all_elementor_postmeta_on_clone()` — Bug 4 fix (catch-all for any `_elementor_*` meta)
- `kp_verify_and_fix_kit()` — post-clone verification + auto-retry at T+15s

Hook setup (triple safety):
```php
add_action('wu_duplicate_site',          'kp_run_complete_clone_fix', 5);     // PRIMARY (WP Ultimo)
add_action('mucd_after_copy_data',       'kp_run_complete_clone_fix', 10, 2); // FALLBACK (manual MUCD)
add_action('wu_pending_site_published',  'kp_run_complete_clone_fix', 9999);  // SAFETY NET
```

---

## Why this is urgent

We're losing customers. Every broken clone = customer support ticket + refund risk. PR #803 was a great start but doesn't cover the postmeta layer. Once you integrate this, I retire 2 mu-plugins from our stack (the patch + a defensive backup layer).

Happy to test any branch you put up. Can also provide more production logs / screenshots if useful.

Thanks David — your work on Multisite Ultimate is what makes our SaaS possible.

— Kenedy / KursoPro

title: fix: Cypress E2E setup tests failing on all branches — wp-env CLI commands exit non-zero
body:
## Problem

The Cypress E2E test suite (`000-setup.spec.js`) is failing consistently on **every branch and every PR**, including `main`. This has been the case for at least the last 6 CI runs across multiple branches.

### Failure pattern

Of the 6 tests in `000-setup.spec.js`, the first 2 pass and the remaining 4 fail:

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Install database tables and mark setup complete | ✅ pass |
| Create a test product/plan | ✅ pass |
| Create a checkout form and registration page | ❌ fail |
| Enable the manual gateway | ❌ fail |
| Disable email verification and enable sync site publish | ❌ fail |
| Reset password strength to default | ❌ fail |

### Root cause

All 4 failing tests invoke `cy.wpCli()` or `cy.wpCliFile()` (defined in `tests/e2e/cypress/support/commands/index.js:5-22`), which run:

```
npx wp-env run tests-cli wp eval "..."
npx wp-env run tests-cli wp eval-file <path>
```

These `cy.exec()` calls exit with code 1. The only Stderr captured is a Node TLS warning — the actual PHP error from the container is not surfaced. Since the table install and product creation succeed, the plugin loads and its core functions work, but the settings-related calls (`wu_save_setting`, `wu_get_setting`) and the checkout form fixture script fail silently.

### Affected files

- `tests/e2e/cypress/integration/000-setup.spec.js` — the failing spec
- `tests/e2e/cypress/support/commands/index.js:5-22` — `wpCli` and `wpCliFile` custom commands
- `tests/e2e/cypress/fixtures/setup-checkout-form.php` — fixture that fails on eval-file
- `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` — the CI workflow
- `.wp-env.json` — wp-env configuration

### Evidence

Cypress failures on `main` (identical pattern on every recent run):
- Run 24410454442 (main) — 4 of 6 fail
- Run 24410261520 (main) — 4 of 6 fail  
- Run 24409522750 (main) — 4 of 6 fail

### Investigation pointers

1. **Stderr swallowed**: `wp-env run tests-cli` likely writes PHP errors to the container's error log, not to stderr that Cypress captures. The `cy.exec()` only sees a Node TLS warning, hiding the real error. Adding `2>&1` or checking container logs post-failure would surface the actual PHP error.

2. **Settings functions may depend on DB state from prior test**: The first test installs tables and marks setup complete. The second creates a product. The third test (`setup-checkout-form.php`) creates a checkout form — this may depend on state (e.g., a product existing with a specific ID, or the setup wizard completion flag) that the prior steps set inconsistently.

3. **`wp eval` quoting in CI**: The inline PHP strings use nested single quotes inside double quotes (`"wu_save_setting('active_gateways', ['manual']);"`). Shell escaping through `npx → wp-env → docker exec → wp eval` may mangle the PHP. The working tests use `eval-file` with a fixture PHP file, which avoids this quoting chain. However, `setup-checkout-form.php` (eval-file) also fails, so quoting isn't the only issue.

4. **Plugin not network-activated in tests container**: `.wp-env.json` lists the plugin in `plugins: ["."]` but wp-env may not network-activate it by default. The table install test works because it calls the installer directly, but `wu_save_setting()` depends on the plugin being fully bootstrapped. Check whether the plugin is network-activated in the tests environment.

### Suggested fix approach

1. Add a debug step to the workflow that runs `npx wp-env run tests-cli wp plugin list --status=active` and `npx wp-env run tests-cli wp eval "var_dump(function_exists('wu_save_setting'));"` to verify plugin bootstrap state.
2. Capture container error logs on failure: `docker logs $(docker ps -q --filter "name=tests-wordpress") 2>&1 | tail -50`.
3. If the plugin isn't network-activated, add `npx wp-env run tests-cli wp plugin activate ultimate-multisite --network` before the Cypress tests.
4. Consider moving all inline `wp eval` calls to fixture PHP files (like the first two tests do) to avoid shell quoting issues through the `npx → wp-env → docker` chain.

title: Template selection  field needs to be added to each pre-configured checkout form
body:
Ultimate multisite has 3 pre-configured checkout forms that make it easier to create checkout forms instead of starting from scratch. Each of them should have the template selection field so that template sites will be used when creating customer sites. 

The out of box experience needs to be that the automatically created checkout form has a template selection field so that when the checkout form is used the template site is used. This template selection field should be configured to show all available templates.

fix: orphan pending_site after membership cancellation — site never provisioned
body:
## What

When a membership transitions to `cancelled` (e.g. the ~2s watchdog timeout), the `pending_site` stored in `wu_membershipmeta` is never deleted. If the customer retries checkout successfully (WC order completes, Stripe subscription active), no code reclaims the orphaned `pending_site` — the customer pays and gets no site.

## Why

Production incident: customer `ladyhellsadm@gmail.com`, Membership ID 479 auto-cancelled at 09:35:14 with pending_site "Cora" orphaned in meta. WC order 61483 completed ($0 with 100% coupon), WCS subscription 61484 active. Expected: site provisioned. Actual: nothing.

## How

- EDIT: `inc/models/class-membership.php` — hook `wu_membership_status_changed`, when new status is `cancelled` and `has_pending_site()` is true, store the pending_site data in a 24h transient keyed by customer email hash (`wu_transferable_pending_` . md5($email)), then call `delete_pending_site()`. This makes the site reclaimable by a retry flow rather than permanently orphaned.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. When a membership transitions to `cancelled`, the pending_site meta is removed from the membership
2. The pending_site data is preserved in a transient for 24 hours, keyed by customer email
3. Unit test confirms pending_site is cleaned up on cancellation
4. Unit test confirms transient is set with correct key and TTL

title: fix: duplicate WP users created on checkout retry — get_user_by check missing
body:
## What

On checkout retry, `wp_insert_user()` is called without a prior `get_user_by('email')` check. This creates duplicate `wp_users` rows with identical `user_email`, only one linked to `wu_customers`. The second orphans the signup flow.

## Why

Production case: two `wp_users` rows (ID 592 and 593) with identical email, only one linked to the customer record. The duplicate user breaks the checkout flow because the customer association is ambiguous.

## How

- EDIT: `inc/checkout/class-checkout.php` — before the `wp_insert_user()` call, add a `get_user_by('email', $user_data['user_email'])` check. If a user already exists with that email, return the existing user ID instead of creating a new one.
- Model on WordPress core's `register_new_user()` which does this check.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. When checkout runs for an email that already exists in `wp_users`, the existing user is reused
2. No duplicate `wp_users` rows are created for the same email
3. The existing user is correctly linked to the `wu_customers` record
4. Unit test confirms duplicate prevention

title: fix: reclaim orphan pending_site on WC order completion
body:
## What

When a WooCommerce order completes for a customer that has a cancelled membership with an orphaned `pending_site`, no code picks up and provisions the site. The customer completes payment but gets nothing.

This is the counterpart to the orphan-cleanup fix — that fix stores the pending_site in a transient on cancellation; this fix reclaims it when a new order succeeds.

## Why

Same production incident as the orphan pending_site bug. Even after the orphan is preserved in a transient, nothing currently listens for WC order completion to reclaim and provision the site.

## How

- EDIT: `inc/checkout/class-checkout.php` or a new hook in the gateway manager — hook `woocommerce_order_status_completed`. Look up the transient `wu_transferable_pending_` . md5(billing_email). If found, create/reactivate a membership, attach the pending_site, publish it, link the order via `_wu_membership_id` postmeta, and delete the transient.
- Alternatively, this could live in `inc/managers/class-membership-manager.php` as a dedicated recovery method.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. When a WC order completes and a matching orphan transient exists, the pending_site is reclaimed
2. A new membership is created or reactivated with the pending_site attached
3. The pending_site is published (blog created)
4. The transient is deleted after successful reclaim
5. Unit test confirms the full reclaim flow

title: fix: JS checkout validator missing i18n strings — hardcoded English fallbacks
body:
## What

In `checkout.min.js`, the validator falls back to hardcoded English strings (e.g. `"%s is required."`) when translations are missing from the `wu_checkout.i18n` object. The `.pot` file has these strings but they are never passed to `wp_localize_script()`.

Missing keys: `field_required`, `field_invalid_email`, `field_min_length`, `field_max_length`, `field_alpha_dash`, `field_lowercase`, `field_same`, `field_integer`, `field_accepted`, `weak_password`, `password_required`, `login_failed`, `sign_in`, `logging_in`, `email_exists`.

## Why

On `es_ES` sites (and any non-English locale), checkout validation messages display in English even when translations exist in the `.mo` file. The strings are in the `.pot` but never localized into `wu_checkout.i18n`.

## How

- EDIT: `inc/class-scripts.php` — in the method that calls `wp_localize_script()` for `wu_checkout`, add all the missing i18n keys listed above, wrapping each in `__('...', 'ultimate-multisite')`.
- Reference the JS source to confirm the exact key names expected.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. All 15 listed i18n keys are present in the `wu_checkout.i18n` localized object
2. Each value uses `__()` with the `ultimate-multisite` text domain
3. Checkout validation messages display in the site's locale when translations exist
4. No hardcoded English fallback is needed for these strings

title: fix: default minimum_password_strength too strict — super_strong rejects reasonable passwords
body:
## What

The default `minimum_password_strength` setting is `super_strong` (zxcvbn score 4), which rejects passwords that most users consider reasonable. Commercial SaaS sites lose signups when the password bar is too high.

## Why

UX friction: users abandon checkout because their normal passwords are rejected. Score 4 is appropriate for banking, not a WordPress multisite signup.

## How

- EDIT: the settings registration (likely in `inc/managers/class-settings-manager.php` or equivalent) — change the default value for `minimum_password_strength` from `super_strong` to `strong` (zxcvbn score 3).
- This only changes the default for new installs; existing installs keep their configured value.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. New installs default to `strong` (score 3) instead of `super_strong` (score 4)
2. Existing installs are not affected (migration not needed — just a default change)
3. The setting UI still offers all options including `super_strong`

title: Ultimate Multisite was testing SES by calling the wrong URL, so AWS returned 404 Not Found before IAM permissions really mattered.
body: SES v2 endpoints include /v2/email/.... AWS documents the test/account endpoint as GET /v2/email/account, sending as POST /v2/email/outbound-emails, and identities as /v2/email/identities. Ultimate Multisite was calling /v2/account and /v2/email-identities, which are not valid SES v2 routes.

title: enable_email_verification=always not working as intended
body: Your Ultimate Multisite setting is enable_email_verification=always, and the customer is still pending. But Stripe marked the membership active, and Ultimate Multisite’s membership status hook published the pending site as soon as the membership became active.

title: t531: fix(checkout): password fields and strength meter broken after inline login popup + email change
body:
## What

After the inline login popup appears (user enters an existing email) and the user then changes the email address, the regular checkout password field stops responding and the strength meter no longer updates.

## Why

**Root cause: Vue 2 DOM element reuse across a `v-if` boundary.**

The inline login prompt wrapper uses `v-if="show_login_prompt && login_prompt_field === 'email'"`. When `show_login_prompt` transitions `true → false` the DOM order of sibling `<div>` wrappers is:

- Before (prompt visible): `email-div` → `login-prompt-div` → `password-div`
- After (prompt hidden): `email-div` → `password-div`

Vue 2's virtual-DOM differ sees two same-tag `<div>` siblings where there were three. With no `key` on the wrappers, Vue recycles `login-prompt-div`'s real DOM node and patches it with the password field's VNode, then removes the original `password-div`. This creates a **new** `#field-password` `<input>` element.

`init_password_strength()` bound its `keyup/input/change` listeners to the **old** `#field-password` element (now detached). The new element has no listeners, so the strength meter never fires and `valid_password` stays `false`, blocking form submission.

## How

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: assets/js/wu-password-strength.js` — add `destroy()` method to `WU_PasswordStrength.prototype` that calls `.off('keyup input change')` on `pass1`/`pass2` and `clearInterval` on the autofill poll
- `EDIT: assets/js/checkout.js:1565-1568` — replace the simple `!this.password_strength_checker` guard in `updated()` with a stale-element check: compare `checker.options.pass1[0]` to the current `jQuery('#field-password')[0]`; if they differ, call `checker.destroy()`, null it, and re-init

### Reference pattern

Follow the existing `init_password_strength()` pattern at `assets/js/checkout.js:1085` and the `WU_PasswordStrength.prototype` object at `assets/js/wu-password-strength.js:87`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Typing in the password field updates the strength meter after the inline login popup has been shown and the email address subsequently changed
- No duplicate event listeners on the password field (destroy cleans up before re-init)
- Existing password strength behaviour unchanged when no inline login prompt interaction occurs

title: Bug: Orphan pending_site after gateway timeout (high priority)
body:
## Bug Report: Orphan pending_site after gateway timeout

**Priority:** High

**Source:** Reported by contributor `superdav42` in a usage session; routed here from `Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite-site-exporter#46` (contributor-insight triage).

## Description

When a signup pre-creates a membership in `pending` state and the user doesn't complete the payment step within ~2s, the watchdog cancels the membership — leaving an orphaned `pending_site` record without a corresponding active membership.

**Note:** The full bug report was captured via `/aidevops-save-todo` in a live session and was partially truncated during automated extraction. The contributor reported 3 production bugs total; this is bug #1 (highest priority). Bugs #2 and #3 could not be fully extracted from the session log due to truncation.

## Reproduction

1. Begin a network site signup flow that pre-creates a `pending` membership
2. Do NOT complete the payment step
3. Wait ~2+ seconds for the watchdog to fire
4. Observe: watchdog cancels the membership, but the `pending_site` record remains

## Expected Behavior

When the watchdog cancels a pending membership, any associated `pending_site` records should also be cleaned up (or the watchdog timeout should be extended past typical payment provider response times).

## Actual Behavior

`pending_site` record is orphaned — no associated active membership exists, but the site record persists in the database.

## Impact

- Orphaned `pending_site` records accumulate over time
- May cause confusion in site listing/management screens
- May block re-registration attempts for the same domain

## Context

Routed from contributor-insight triage: `Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite-site-exporter#46`
